audit_scope.description: Trust model analysis for EIP-145 (bitwise shift instructions), EIP-3554 (difficulty bomb delay), Cancun fork state transition/transaction validation/gas economics/withdrawals, and EIP-7623 (calldata gas floor). Covers EVM opcode execution, block state transitions, transaction validation, beacon chain withdrawal processing, and calldata gas pricing.

in_scope: Block state transition and validation (Cancun fork)
Transaction validation including blob transaction checks
Gas economics: EIP-1559 base fee, blob gas pricing

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers propagate blocks via the P2P network. They are untrusted and may send invalid blocks. The EL performs complete block validation including header checks (sequential block numbers, timestamp ordering, gas constraints, base fee, PoS fields), body execution, and Merkle root verification. Invalid blocks raise InvalidBlock exceptions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transaction submitters are unauthenticated external users or applications. Transactions undergo comprehensive pre-execution validation: nonce matching, balance sufficiency, sender is EOA, fee structure validation, and blob transaction field checks (KZG 0x01 versioned hash, blob presence, gas limits). Invalid transactions are rejected with specific error types.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain (Consensus Layer)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (withdrawal list in execution payload)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The Beacon Chain communicates with the EL via the Engine API, authenticated with JWT. Withdrawal data is trusted beyond format checks - the EL credits balances based on CL-provided withdrawal lists without independent verification of validator eligibility. This is semi-trusted because the Engine API uses JWT authentication and the CL has its own consensus mechanisms, but a compromised CL could credit arbitrary balances.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter (Calldata)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Entities submitting transactions with calldata are untrusted. EIP-7623 introduces a gas floor for calldata-heavy transactions (10 gas per token vs standard 4), making data-heavy transactions 2.5x more expensive. This mitigates calldata-based DoS by ensuring data-heavy transactions pay proportionally for the block space they consume.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All blocks from peers undergo full state transition validation: header validation (consensus rules), body execution (all transactions processed), and Merkle root verification (transactions, receipts, withdrawals, state roots must match header). Blocks failing any check are rejected with InvalidBlock. The client retains 255+ blocks for reorg handling.

Transactions undergo comprehensive check_transaction() validation: nonce match, sufficient balance (including blob gas fees), sender is EOA, EIP-1559 fee parameter validity, and for blob transactions: KZG 0x01 versioned hash format, blob count within limits, blob gas limits. Intrinsic gas must be sufficient.

Withdrawal data from the Beacon Chain is authenticated via JWT on the Engine API. The EL processes withdrawals by converting Gwei amounts to Wei and crediting recipient balances. The EL does NOT independently verify validator eligibility or withdrawal amounts - this trust is placed in the CL consensus. A compromised CL could cause unauthorized balance increases.

Calldata-heavy transactions are subject to the gas floor: max(standard_gas, 21000 + 10 * tokens_in_calldata). This ensures data-heavy transactions pay at least 10 gas per calldata token (vs standard 4), preventing cheap calldata flooding. Transaction gas limits must meet the floor requirement or be rejected.
